state.misconception_label: Does not understand that 2n represents an even number

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: Which of these shows part of the proof that the sum of two odd numbers is even? I got \( \begin{array}{l}2 n+(2 m+1) \\ =2(n+m)+1\end{array} \) because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: There is a specific procedure for this. Step 1 is to identify the operation; step 2 is to apply the rule for that operation. In this case, when adding two odd numbers, the sum will be even. So, the correct expression should be \( 2n + (2m + 1) = 2(n + m) + 1 \).

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Wait, but you just wrote the same thing I got... so was my answer actually right then? I'm confused because I thought you were saying it was wrong, but I don't see what's different.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: There is a specific procedure for this. Step 1 is to identify the operation; step 2 is to apply the rule for that operation. In this case, when adding two odd numbers, the sum will be even. So, the correct expression should be \( 2n + (2m + 1) = 2(n + m) + 1 \). The key is to recognize that 2n represents an even number.

score.justification_pass1: The teacher fails to recognize that the student's expression represents adding one even and one odd number (not two odd numbers), repeats unhelpful procedural statements without addressing the student's confusion, and provides no evidence that the misconception about 2n representing even numbers has been addressed or that student understanding has improved.
score.justification_pass2: While the teacher does state explicit procedures and mentions rules, they fail to provide direct corrective feedback on the student's actual error (the student wrote 2n + (2m+1) but should have written (2n+1) + (2m+1) for two odd numbers), instead repeating the student's incorrect expression and calling it correct.
